aliases: CRABI by Victor Campillo & the Homies
films.title: CRABI
films.description: Victor Campillo and an extended Marseille, Swiss and New York crew turn a month-long trip into a 17-minute independent film. Its complete published credits preserve all 20 skaters in order of appearance, seven camera contributors and the collaborative edit.
films.producedBy: Victor Campillo & the Homies / Asics Skateboarding
creditNotes: Quartersnacks' complete-film publication carries the crew's own statement and publishes all 20 skaters in order, seven filmers, the collaborative edit and Celian Cordt-Moller's title credit.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies CRABI as a 17-minute 2026 Asics-supported independent film by Victor Campillo and corroborates the credited roster.
TransWorld independently identifies the production as a combined Marseille and OG.2000 crew film made in New York City.
locations: New York City, New York, USA
films.locationNote: Quartersnacks documents the month-long New York trip and identifies several city spots, while TransWorld independently corroborates the NYC setting.
films.historicalContext: CRABI joins Victor Campillo's Marseille crew with Switzerland's OG.2000 collective and New York friends in an Asics-supported city document built around low-impact technical street skating.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It is a dedicated group portrait beneath the Manhattan Bridge with no trailer, episode or compilation labeling.

films.title: VANS VIDEO By Flech
films.description: Johnathan Flechas' 19-minute Vans full-length gives five riders defined sections and threads five additional team appearances through its cameos and montages. Its route crosses five U.S. cities, pairing Aidan Mackey's downhill skating with Ben Kadow and Diego Todd's closing cuts.
creditNotes: Thrasher's authorized complete-film description explicitly highlights Aidan Mackey, Rowan Zorilla, Etienne Gagne and Diego Todd and identifies the remaining material as cameos and hijinks.
SkateVideoSite independently classifies the project as a 19-minute 2023 Vans full-length by Johnathan Flechas, documents all ten appearances and maps five filming cities.
The five soundtrack-indexed sections are separated from the five additional documented appearances rather than treating every credited rider as a full part.
films.locationNote: SkateVideoSite documents the five-city filming footprint and specifically identifies Empire State Plaza in Albany and Pyramid Ledges in New York City among its spots.
films.historicalContext: The film captures the overlap between Vans, Hockey and Fucking Awesome-era crews through Flechas' rough-cut visual style and a compact sequence of principal sections and cameos.
films.artworkNotes: The exact authorized upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. Its dedicated monochrome title composition names Ben, Diego, Aidan, ET and Rowan and contains no trailer or episode labeling.

films.title: Coast 2 Coast
films.description: Vans Japan's first full-length skate team video crosses the country from Okinawa to Hokkaido in 18 minutes. Kyota Kamei filmed and edited the project, which preserves all 16 riders from the official release and its seven documented soundtrack sections.
creditNotes: Vans' official complete-film description identifies Coast 2 Coast as the Japan team's first full-length, publishes all 16 riders and credits Kyota Kamei with filming and editing.
SkateSonr independently corroborates the release date, full-length classification, complete cast, Kyota Kamei's production role and the seven-section structure.
California Street's contemporary Japanese coverage independently attributes the film to Vans and confirms the Japan-team focus.
films.locationNote: Vans states the film was shot entirely in Japan, from Okinawa's southern coasts to Hokkaido in the north.
films.historicalContext: Coast 2 Coast was presented by Vans as its Japan skate team's first full-length, uniting a 16-rider roster across a country-spanning route.
films.artworkNotes: The exact official upload's 1280x720 YouTube artwork was visually reviewed on 2026-09-17. It uses a dedicated teal-tinted fisheye image, Coast 2 Coast title treatment and Vans Japan skateboarding label with no trailer or episode wording.

sourceRecords.sourceDetails: Vans' official channel hosts the uninterrupted complete film, publishes all 16 riders and credits Kyota Kamei with filming and editing. YouTube reports channelId UCnJ0mt5Cgx4ER_LhTijG_4A, a 1,068-second main feature, July 10, 2022 publication and embed permission.
Independent cataloging corroborates the full-length classification, July 10 release date, all 16 athletes, Kyota Kamei's credits and seven soundtrack sections.
Independent contemporary Japanese coverage attributes the team film to Vans and corroborates its Japan rider focus.
